question: Approximate Zillow's Free Cash Flow as CFO - Capex. What was the trend of FCF margin from FY2022 to FY2024?
answer:
2024: 12.7%
2023: 11.3%
2022: 24.8%

FCF margin has declined substantially since 2022 and seems to have settled into a new normal of low teens percent.

model_answer:
Using **CFO − purchases of property & equipment** (USD millions):

| | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Cash flow from operations | $4,504 | $354 | $428 |
| Capex (PP&E purchases) | $(115) | $(135) | $(143) |
| **Approx. FCF** | **$4,389** | **$219** | **$285** |
| Revenue | $1,958 | $1,945 | $2,236 |
| **FCF margin** | **~224%** | **~11.3%** | **~12.7%** |

**Trend:** FCF margin collapsed from an anomalous ~224% in FY2022 to ~11% in FY2023, then improved modestly to ~13% in FY2024. The FY2022 figure is distorted by roughly **$3.9 billion of inventory liquidation** as Zillow wound down its iBuying operations, which massively inflated CFO. Excluding that, FY2022 FCF margin would have been far lower—roughly mid-20s%. So the meaningful trend is: **a huge 2022-to-2023 normalization downward, followed by a small 2024 recovery driven by 15% revenue growth and CFO up 21% while capex rose only ~6%.**

If intangible purchases ($25M, $30M, $28M) are also treated as capex, FCF would be **$4,364M / $189M / $257M**, or margins of **~223% / ~9.7% / ~11.5%**—same trend.

Sources: [Zillow FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1617640/000161764025000016/z-20241231.htm), [FY2024 earnings release](https://investors.zillowgroup.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2025/Zillow-Group-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2024-Financial-Results/default.aspx).
judge_reason: Contradiction triggered by stated FY2022 FCF margin ~224% versus official 24.8%, despite otherwise matching margins/trend.
